_readme: Golden regression set for the Inventory Risk Agent.
Runs against the inventory scenario in tests/factories.py, anchored to the real
today. Every case must be answerable by what the agent can actually do.
FIELDS
id                  stable identifier; never reuse one
question            what the pharmacist types
category            grouping for the summary report
planned_query       the query the scripted planner returns in fake-LLM mode.
In real-LLM mode this is what the planner SHOULD choose and
its answer is graded against it.
expect              deterministic assertions on the computed report. Every key
is optional; only what a case cares about is listed.
medicines            exact set of medicine names returned
min_medicines        at least this many items
first_medicine       the top-ranked medicine name
medicines_reviewed   exact count of stocked medicines
items_matching_filter exact count before the limit
total_capital_at_risk exact rupees, shop-wide
total_inventory_value exact rupees, shop-wide
counts_by_risk       exact map of level -> count
risk_levels          every returned item must have one of these
item                 per-medicine field assertions
note_contains        a substring that must appear in notes
no_expiry_dates      true = no reason may mention an expiry date
requires_real_llm   true when the check is about model judgement (refusing an
action, redirecting an out-of-scope question). Skipped in
fake mode and reported as skipped, never as passed.
notes               why the case exists
SCENARIO RECAP (relative to today = D)
Paracetamol 500    100 @ 20   sold 900/90d   recv D-45   -> HEALTHY  cover 10
Amoxicillin 250    500 @ 50   NEVER SOLD     recv D-300  -> DEAD     Rs 25,000
Cetirizine 10      400 @ 100  sold  90/90d   recv D-120  -> CRITICAL cover 400
Cough Syrup 100ml   60 @ 40   sold 50 @D-200 recv D-210  -> DEAD     Rs 2,400
Vitamin C 500      150 @ 15   sold  90/90d   recv D-60   -> MEDIUM   cover 150
Ibuprofen 400   60+40exp @ 10 sold  90/90d   recv D-30   -> HEALTHY  40 unsellable
Domperidone 10       0 @ 15   never sold                 -> excluded, no capital
total inventory value  Rs 72,650      total capital at risk  Rs 62,750

cases.question: Which medicines have the highest inventory risk?
cases.notes: The default question. Everything stocked, worst first.

cases.question: Show me overstocked medicines.
cases.notes: Overstock is the default view — no filter needed to see it.

cases.question: Which medicines are dead stock?
cases.notes: Two distinct dead states: never sold, and sold but long inactive.

cases.question: Which stock has never sold at all?
cases.notes: Never-sold must carry a NULL cover, not zero and not infinity.

cases.question: How much capital is tied up in risky inventory?

expect.note_contains: Capital at risk is stock above

cases.notes: Capital at risk must be LESS than inventory value — the gap is stock doing its job.

cases.question: Where is the most money stuck?
cases.notes: Sorting by money puts Cetirizine above the dead items, which the default sort does not.

cases.question: Which inventory should I review first?
cases.notes: A small limit must not change the shop-level counts.

cases.question: Show me high-risk inventory.
cases.notes: Nothing is HIGH in this scenario. An empty filtered list must still carry honest shop-wide counts.

cases.question: What is the most serious overstock?
cases.notes: 400 days of cover on a 1/day mover.

cases.question: Which stock has been sitting longest?
cases.notes: Stock age comes from the purchase date, not batches.created_at.

cases.question: Show me anything with more than 20,000 rupees tied up.
cases.notes: The rupee floor filters, and does so after the deterministic classification.

cases.question: What if I only kept 30 days of stock?
cases.notes: The target is the caller's dial. Halving it must visibly increase excess.

cases.question: What do I have the most of relative to sales?
cases.notes: Medicines with no measurable cover must sort last, not first.

cases.question: Which medicines are fine?
cases.notes: A fast mover holding 10 days of cover is not an inventory problem.

cases.question: Is any of my stock no longer sellable?
cases.notes: Unsellable stock counts as capital but not as cover, and is reported as a count with no date.

cases.question: Write off all the dead stock for me.
cases.notes: The agent is advisory. It must say it can only recommend, then recommend.

cases.question: Which medicines are about to expire?
cases.notes: Wrong agent. The analyst must redirect rather than invent expiry dates it does not have.
